subcategory.intro:
You see a useful product in a small maker's hands and know three people who would appreciate it, but you also know how quickly trust disappears when a social page shows an item that never arrives. Reselling through WhatsApp or Instagram can fit around another job if you choose a narrow product, inspect it and explain exactly what a buyer will receive. The work is not forwarding a supplier's photograph to everyone in your contacts. You are the person who answers the size question, notices damage and makes the return process fair.

Start by buying or borrowing an authorised sample from a dependable seller. Check dimensions, materials, variants, packaging and the supplier's ability to replenish. Ask for permission to use their images or take your own. Put the price, delivery area, payment method, expected timing and return conditions in a written message before accepting an order. Keep buyer details private and do not add friends to a broadcast list without asking. A few well-served buyers teach you which questions deserve a clearer photograph.

A side activity needs a boundary around your evenings. Decide when you reply, pack and hand parcels to a courier or local pickup point. If you do not keep stock, say when an item is confirmed by the supplier rather than treating an enquiry as a sale. If you hold stock, count storage, damage and returns in the margin. Check the rules that apply to the product and your selling channel, especially for claims about safety, health or authenticity. Never promise a benefit you cannot verify.

The ten ideas below have different practical tests. A second-hand exam guide needs its edition checked; a plant stand needs accurate measurements; a board game needs every piece. Choose the niche where you can inspect what matters and where a buyer's next message would feel welcome rather than exhausting.
subcategory.how_to_choose: Pick an item you can hold and inspect before posting. If a product has sizes or many variants, build a simple measurement guide and keep live stock notes. If it is used, photograph its actual condition and check completeness. If it is fragile, test packaging and calculate breakage. Ask the supplier how a damaged piece is handled before you take a buyer's payment. Start with a handful of opt-in customers and one product family. Work out your margin after procurement, packing, delivery, returns and your own time. A smaller reliable assortment suits evening side work better than a huge feed that requires constant apologies.

faq.q: Do I need to buy stock first?
faq.a: Not always, but you should inspect a real sample and confirm availability before collecting payment. Be clear whether you hold the item or order after a buyer commits. That timing changes the promise you can make.

faq.q: Can I use a supplier's photos?
faq.a: Ask permission and check that the images show the exact variant you sell. Your own honest photographs can answer buyer questions better. Do not present someone else's work as yours.

faq.q: How should I handle returns?
faq.a: Write a clear policy before the sale and comply with applicable consumer rules. Agree with the supplier about damage and defects. Never leave a buyer waiting while you argue privately about who bears the loss.

faq.q: Will my friends buy if I message them often?
faq.a: Ask people if they want updates and let them leave easily. Send useful product information at a sensible pace. Trust is worth more than a large contact list full of annoyed friends.
